dialect.detail: Uses VALUE OF FILE-ID clause and PROGRAM-ID AS alias syntax typical of Micro Focus or ACUCOBOL; ASSIGN TO DISK with VALUE OF FILE-ID is a Micro Focus/ACUCOBOL idiom. GOBACK used as main program terminator.
evidence: ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE with RELATIVE KEY

purpose.domain_detail: University student scheduling system - displays a student's class schedule from indexed/relative files
purpose.summary: This program opens four indexed/relative files (course section, student master, course enrollment, course master) and prompts the user to enter a student ID. It then reads the student's enrollment chain and displays their class schedule including CRN, section, course code, title, and credit hours.

notable_features: VALUE OF FILE-ID clause for file assignment (Micro Focus/ACUCOBOL style)
Linked-list style enrollment chain traversal via CE-STUDENT-NEXT pointer
ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE file with RELATIVE KEY
Multiple COPY statements for file record layouts
Condition CE-DROPPED NOT = "D" OR "D" (likely a logic bug)
verdict.notes: The program is clearly a student exercise (filename STUDENT-SCHEDULE.cbl, programmer name in header, 'OBJECTIVE: 11' comment, university domain). The condition 'IF CE-DROPPED NOT = "D" OR "D"' is almost certainly a logic error (always true or always false). The IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header is missing (only PROGRAM-ID present). Dialect is likely Micro Focus or ACUCOBOL based on VALUE OF FILE-ID and ASSIGN TO DISK idioms.
